newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative chairman sees election in 6 months.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative chairman sees election in 6 months.

text.p: The chairman of Britain's ruling Conservative Party has forecast on Thursday that the next general election is some six months away.
Brian Mawhinney makes the prediction in The House Magazine, a publication circulated to MPs and parliamentary journalists and lobbyists.

Writing of next week's Conservative Party conference which begins on Tuesday, Mawhinney says: "With a probably six months still to go between the Conference and the Election, no-one will expect us to reveal the full contents of our manifesto. But some appetising tasters can be predicted."
An election must be called by May next year -- seven months away -- and most commentators have assumed Prime Minister John Major would wait until the last possible moment before going to the country.
In his article, Mawhinney outs a brave face on opinion polls showing the Conservatives trailing the opposition Labour Party under leader Tony Blair by more than 20 percentage points.
"Mr Blair has peaked -- and it's downhill all the way for him now," he said.
Writing in the same magazine, Major says the conference season "will be the launchpad for the next election campaign."
He says the next government will inherit the strongest economy in Britain for generations.

"The first choice is an economic one -- whether we turn Britain into the Enterprise Centre of Europe, forging ahead in today's competitive markets, or whether we trust a party with a track record of bringing Britain to a standstill and throw away the opportunities ahead," he writes. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
